status: draft: no page or module loads this file
note: Application-defined mappings from an ordered sequence of sign labels to a stored English sentence. This is not translation, and a sequence listed here is not claimed to be a grammatical sentence of American Sign Language. No fluent signer has reviewed the sequences, their order or the English outputs.
labelNote: A sign is named in signs by its label id: the word recognizer's label in upper case with single spaces (I / ME, THANK YOU, FOOD, FINISH). display is the name shown to the user. An alias is another name for the same sign and is replaced by its label id before matching. FOOD and EAT are one sign: 20 names, 19 signs.
outputNote: A match gives the phrase id, english, and glosses (one written gloss per sign, in order). glossLine is the same sequence as one line for display, with a question mark where the phrase is stored as a question.

tiers.A: isolated phone-game recordings of many signers, one-handed
tiers.B: a small number of isolated clips, and sentence segments
tiers.C: sentence segments only; no isolated recording
tiers.D: no isolated recording on disk; a few sentence segments

matching.rule: A phrase matches when the completed sequence of label ids, after aliases are replaced, equals its signs or the signs of one of its variants, in order and in full. Anything else gives no output.
matching.activeOnly: Only phrases with active true may be matched. A phrase is active only while every one of its signs can be demonstrated; PB-08 to PB-15 are inactive until that is decided.
matching.variantOutput: A variant gives the id and english of its phrase and its own glosses.
matching.prefixFreeNote: Checked on 2026-11-14 over the 17 sequences of this file (15 phrases and 2 variants): no sequence is the beginning of another and no two are equal, with or without the inactive phrases. The variants do not break this. A phrase of a single YES, NO, WATER, PLEASE, WHERE, YOU or STOP would break it, so the property has to be checked again whenever a phrase or a variant is added.

FINISH.note: Every model and source file names this sign FINISH; FINISHED is the name shown.

FOOD.note: FOOD and EAT are one sign and one class with two names. The extra-word templates and the 17-word network give the label FOOD; a 19-class list uses the class name EAT / FOOD.

GOOD.note: In no phrase: the one-handed form is a documented look-alike of THANK YOU.

WHAT.note: In no phrase: exchanged with WANT in the records. Where it is used, the sign meant is the open-hand form, not the index finger across the palm.

I / ME.note: One sign for both English words.
